newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac rules out cabinet reshuffle, praises Juppe.
newsitem.headline: Chirac rules out cabinet reshuffle, praises Juppe.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac on Thursday ruled out a cabinet reshuffle despite the worsening unpopularity of Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
"I have no intention of making a cabinet reshuffle," Chirac said in a television interview, praising Juppe as courageous.
Opinion polls show Juppe is the least popular prime minister in modern French history. A poll this week showed that most voters would like him to step down.

"Alain Juppe is leading a difficult and courageous policy. Courageous politicians are rarely popular, but they are necessary," Chirac said, adding he admired Juppe for continuing his task undeterred by unpopularity.

"I have confidence in him to continue these policies," Chirac said in his first extended public statement since July. Juppe's centre-right government has raised taxes and cut public spending to meet budget criteria for the single European currency, while unemployment has climbed to a record 12.6 percent.
Many commentators have speculated that Chirac will order a reshuffle sometime in 1997 to streamline the government before 1998 elections.
